newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Rangebound Bunds to try to break 101.04.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Rangebound Bunds to try to break 101.04.

text.p: LIFFE June Bund futures will remain broadly rangebound for the next few sessions but will try to break to the upside on Wednesday, technical analysts said.

"It looks like the market is trying to stabilise around these levels and we will probably be in a choppy range for a little while," said Charles Diebel, senior technical analyst at Technical Data in London.
"If anything that tends to argue we will go a bit higher from here. First resistance is at 101.04."
At 0706 GMT, June Bund futures were at 100.92, up 16 basis points on the day.
Diebel said the recovery late on Tuesday suggested Bunds were trying to build a base, but until they broke above 101.04, they would still be range trading.
"Short-term momentum is overbought so it doesn't look like we are going to have the strength to break up," he said.
"Basically we are in a corrective target zone of the Fibonacci retracements of the prior upmove in April and May."
The June contract rallied from 99.05 on April 3 to 102.59 on May 14.
Diebel said the 38.2 percent retracement of that rally would act as resistance above 101.04. That level comes in at 101.23.

"To the downside, we are not likely to get below 100.56, but if we do then we are going to 100.40 where the 61.8 percent retracement intersects," he said, adding that those retracement levels should mark the outer boundaries of the trading range for now.
Steve Hutt, technical analyst at NatWest Financial Futures in London, agreed 101.04 would be the key level for the market as it attempted to bounce higher.
"There is also 101.14, which was previous resistance from the middle of April. The band between 101.04 and 101.14 will be important to get through," he said.
"On Tuesday daily candlestick charts showed a hammer formation, which is a reversal signal from the recent bear trend," said Hutt.
He said the Relative Strength Index (RSI) was also looking positive as it had held up over the past four to five days despite trade slipping to 100.63 on May 22 and then 100.56 on Tuesday.
"We had bullish convergence of the RSI so that is a very positive signal," he said.
At the short end September Euromarks were at 96.74, up 0.01 on the day.
